(a) Settlement Fund.—Section 102 of the Fallon Paiute Shoshone Indian Tribes Water Rights Settlement Act of 1990 (Public Law 101–618; 104 Stat. 3289) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (C)—
            (A) in paragraph (1)—
                (i) by striking the matter preceding subparagraph (a) and inserting the following: “Notwithstanding any 
conflicting provision in the original Fund plan during Fund fiscal year 2006 or any subsequent Fund fiscal year, 6 percent of the average quarterly market value of the Fund during the immediately preceding 3 Fund fiscal years (referred to in this title as the ‘Annual 6 percent Amount’), plus any unexpended and unobligated portion of the Annual 6 percent Amount from any of the 3 immediately preceding Fund fiscal years that are subsequent to Fund fiscal year 2005, less any negative income that may accrue on that portion, may be expended or obligated only for the following purposes:”; and  
                (ii) by adding at the end the following: “(g) Fees and expenses incurred in connection with the investment of the Fund, for investment management, investment consulting, custodianship, and other transactional services or matters.”; and   
            (B) by striking paragraph (4) and inserting the following: “(4) No monies from the Fund other than the amounts authorized under paragraphs (1) and (3) may be expended or obligated for any purpose. “(5) Notwithstanding any conflicting provision in the original Fund plan, during Fund fiscal year 2006 and during each subsequent Fund fiscal year, not more than 20 percent of the Annual 6 percent Amount for the Fund fiscal year (referred to in this title as the ‘Annual 1.2 percent Amount’) may be expended or obligated under paragraph (1)(c) for per capita distributions to tribal members, except that during each Fund fiscal year subsequent to Fund fiscal year 2006, any unexpended and unobligated portion of the Annual 1.2 percent Amount from any of the 3 immediately preceding Fund fiscal years that are subsequent to Fund fiscal year 2005, less any negative income that may accrue on that portion, may also be expended or obligated for such per capita payments.”; and   
        (2) in subsection (D), by adding at the end the following: “Notwithstanding any conflicting provision in the original Fund plan, the Fallon Business Council, in consultation with the Secretary, shall promptly amend the original Fund plan for purposes of conforming the Fund plan to this title and making nonsubstantive updates, improvements, or corrections to the original Fund plan.”.   
    (b) Definitions.—Section 107 of the Fallon Paiute Shoshone Indian Tribes Water Rights Settlement Act of 1990 (Public Law 101–618; 104 Stat. 3293) is amended—
        (1) by redesignating subsections (D), (E), (F), and (G) as subsections (F), (G), (H), and (I), respectively; and  
        (2) by striking subsections (B) and (C) and inserting the following: “(B) the term ‘Fund fiscal year’ means a fiscal year of the Fund (as defined in the Fund plan); “(C) the term ‘Fund plan’ means the plan established under section 102(F), including the original Fund plan (the ‘Plan for Investment, Management, Administration and Expenditure dated December 20, 1991’) and all amendments of the Fund plan under subsection (D) or (F)(1) of section 102; “(D) the term ‘income’ means the total net return from the investment of the Fund, consisting of all interest, dividends, realized and unrealized gains and losses, and other earnings, less all related fees and expenses incurred for investment management, investment consulting, custodianship and transactional services or matters; “(E) the term ‘principal’ means the total amount appropriated to the Fallon Paiute Shoshone Tribal Settlement Fund under section 102(B);”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that consultation between a tribal body and the Secretary is participation by an outside party. But here the tribe's Business Council is the decision-maker amending its own Fund plan, and the federal Secretary is merely the one consulted, so no outside party is being brought into a federal decision. The rest of the section only sets spending limits and definitions for the settlement fund, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Fallon Business Council, in consultation with the Secretary, shall promptly amend the original Fund plan for purposes of conforming the Fund plan to this title

opus.w: The consultation runs the wrong way: the tribal Business Council makes the decision (amending its own Fund plan) and consults the federal Secretary. No outside party is consulted before a federal decision. This is like Example 9, where consultation over a tribal or state plan was not participation in a federal decision. The rest of the section only sets spending limits and definitions, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: the Fallon Business Council, in consultation with the Secretary, shall promptly amend the original Fund plan for purposes of conforming the Fund plan to this title and making nonsubstantive updates, improvements, or corrections to the original Fund plan.
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** The phrase "the Fallon Business Council, in consultation with the Secretary" pairs a tribe with a federal official, so it can look like outsider participation.

**Why it fails:** The roles are reversed from what the definition requires. The tribal council is the one deciding: it amends its own Fund plan and consults the Secretary. No outside party is brought into a federal decision. This matches Example 9, where a state or tribal plan was prepared through consultation and that did not count. The rest of the section only sets spending limits and definitions for the Fund.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Fallon Business Council (an outside entity) to amend a fund plan, consulting with the Secretary (a federal official). The definition of participation requires the *federal government* to consult with outside parties before making a decision. Here, the outside entity is making the change and consulting with the federal government, which is the reverse of the defined participation mechanism. Additionally, the amendment is to a specific fund plan managed by the tribe, not a broad federal policy decision made by the government after consulting with the public.
qwen_chat.s: the Fallon Business Council, in consultation with the Secretary, shall promptly amend the original Fund plan
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Fallon Business Council is an outside entity (a tribal government) and that its action to "amend the original Fund plan" constitutes participation in a federal decision. However, the text specifies that the Business Council acts "in consultation with the Secretary." The key question is whether this consultation involves the federal government consulting with outsiders *before* making a decision, or if the outside entity is making the decision (or a part of it) with federal input. Here, the Business Council is the primary actor amending the plan, and the Secretary is consulted. This is the reverse of the definition, which requires the *federal government* to consult with outsiders. Furthermore, the amendment is to a "Fund plan" which is likely an internal management document for the settlement fund, not a broad federal policy decision. More importantly, the definition states: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." In this clause, the *Business Council* is making the amendment, not the Secretary. The Secretary is being consulted by the Council. This is not the federal government consulting with outsiders; it is an outside entity consulting with the federal government. Therefore, it does not fit the definition of participation as defined (federal government consulting with outsiders).

Wait, let's re-read carefully. "the Fallon Business Council, in consultation with the Secretary, shall promptly amend the original Fund plan". The actor is the Business Council. The Secretary is consulted. The definition says: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." Here, the federal government (Secretary) is *being* consulted by the outside entity (Business Council). The definition focuses on the federal government initiating or being required to consult with outsiders. Does the Secretary make a decision here? The text says the Business Council *shall* amend the plan. The Secretary's role is consultative. This is not the federal government consulting with outsiders to make a federal decision. It is a tribal entity making a change to a plan, consulting with the federal government. This is not "participation" under the provided definition, which requires the *federal government* to consult with outsiders.

Another potential trap: Is the "Fund plan" a federal decision? The Fund is a "Tribal Settlement Fund". The plan is for the management of the fund. The Business Council is the governing body of the tribe. The Secretary is the Secretary of the Interior (implied by context of Indian affairs). The Business Council amends the plan. The Secretary is consulted. This is not the federal government consulting with outsiders. It is the opposite.

Therefore, the label is No.
